sentences.text: A perusal of the order would show that the official respondents were directed to demarcate the land of the petitioner Kaushik Gupta if any part of land is acquired for the Highway and thereafter draw the proceeding for payment of compensation under the Act, 2013 to the extent of land acquired from petitioner and after acquisition proceeding, the adequate compensation would be paid in accordance with law.

1 2.
Learned counsel for respondent no.1 opposes the review petition and on instructions, she submits that compensation proceeding has already been carried out and the amount has been paid.
3. Perusal of the order would show that the order will not require any review as the petitioners herein have not pointed out any manifest error on the face of record.

If the petitioners are aggrieved,
they should have taken up the issue in the higher Courts.
Having not done so, this Court in exercise of jurisdiction under Order 47 Rule 1 would not reconsider the issue as it would amount to rehearing.

4. The Supreme Court in a recent decision rendered in Civil Appeal No.3601 of 2020 - Shri Ram Sahu (dead) through Lrs v. Vinod Kumar Rawat decided on 03.11.2020 laid down that Under Order 47 Rule 1 CPC a judgment may be open to review inter alia if there is a mistake or an error apparent on the face of the record.

An error which is not selfevident and has to be detected by a process of reasoning, can hardly be said to be an error apparent on the face of the record justifying the court to exercise its power of review under Order 47 Rule 1 CPC.
In exercise of the jurisdiction under Order 47 Rule 1 CPC it is not permissible for an erroneous decision to be "reheard and corrected".
It is further held that there is a clear distinction between an "erroneous decision" and "error apparent on the face of the record".
While the first can be corrected by the higher forum, the latter can only be corrected by exercise of the review of jurisdiction.
A review petition has a limited purpose and cannot be allowed to be 'an appeal in disguise.
5. In view of the above legal position, I do not find any merit in the review petition warranting interference by this court.
Accordingly, this petition is rejected.
